system_prompt_style.note: CORAL generates a per-worktree CORAL.md instruction file from task config (name, description, tips); the underlying coding agent supplies its own system prompt.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Agents can retrieve and contribute to the shared file system via the CORAL CLI tool ... and directly use Bash tool to access it.
env_context_strategy.note: Quote lightly reflows paper wording; shared memory is symlinked but agents navigate it themselves.

context_compaction.note: Context compaction is handled inside the delegated coding-agent runtime; no evidence in provided CORAL sources.

observation_format.note: Scores/feedback returned as text/JSON files to the agent.

tool_call_format.note: CORAL exposes itself as a CLI (`coral eval`) invoked via the runtime's bash tool; the underlying runtime's own call format is not in CORAL's code.

tool_count.note: Tool count is runtime-dependent; the Pi runtime enumerates 7 tools. Default runtime is claude_code, whose tool set is not defined in CORAL.

edit_primitive.note: Edit primitives belong to the delegated runtime; inferred from edit/write tool names.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: a skills-first bundle (no MCP) that teaches the workflows (`coral setup` → `init`/`validate` → `start`/`status`/`log`)
tool_schema_source.note: CORAL ships a CLI plus hand-written skills rather than machine-generated tool schemas.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Spawn agents → agents read CORAL.md → commit changes → eval runs → repeat

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: periodically prompting the agents to exercise self-reflection and pivoting for new ideas when existing approaches plateau
planning_granularity.note: Heartbeat prompts steer strategy; no stored structured plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: coordination between agents occurs primarily through shared persistent memory
multi_agent_topology.note: N symmetric agents in parallel worktrees; a manager issues heartbeat prompts but does not decompose tasks.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: As agents generate attempts, notes, and skills, they write artifacts
delegation_mechanism.note: Closest value: indirect coordination via a shared filesystem rather than a true message bus; no task delegation.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: CORAL manages the full lifecycle: creating isolated workspaces, generating agent instructions, running evaluations, and collecting results.
human_in_loop.note: No approval gate documented in the run loop; humans start/stop runs and monitor via `coral ui`.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: scoped attempts, notes, skills, heartbeat state, and migration between islands

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: skills/ records reusable procedures, tools, scripts, and implementation patterns transferable across attempts.
long_term_memory.note: notes/ = file_notes; skills/ = skill_library; attempts/ is an episodic record on the filesystem.

self_verification.evidence_quote: A grader daemon scores every commit.
self_verification.note: Graders are harness-run; rubric LLM-judge graders shipped; heartbeat reflect prompts drive self-critique.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Agents continue the loop, building on useful results while exploring alternatives in parallel.
retry_policy.note: Open-ended: agents keep submitting attempts to maximize the score; no fixed attempt cap by default.

rollback.evidence_quote: Each agent runs in its own git worktree.
rollback.note: Attempts are commits in per-agent worktrees, so prior states are recoverable via git.

termination_condition.note: max_turns default 0 = unlimited; runs otherwise end when the operator stops them (`coral stop`) or the agent process exits.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: LiteLLM gateway configuration for intercepting agent model traffic.
cost_controls.note: Gateway allows per-model routing/budgeting; explicit budget fields not visible in the truncated config.

timeouts.evidence_quote: timeout: int = 300  # eval timeout in seconds (0 = no limit)
timeouts.note: Per-eval (grader) timeout; no run-level wall-clock cap seen.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Spawn and manage Pi coding agent CLI subprocesses.
execution_isolation.note: Agents run as host subprocesses in git worktrees; a Docker session mode and OS sandbox provider are available.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: each agent runs as an unprivileged user (manager and grader stay root), so agents can no longer read `.coral/private/`
filesystem_access.note: Worktree isolation plus private grader directory hidden from agents; on host, user isolation is opt-in via agents.isolate_user.

network_policy.evidence_quote: which enforces filesystem and network boundaries — uniformly across all runtimes
network_policy.note: Sandbox with network boundaries exists but is a configurable provider; default run is unrestricted.

permission_model.evidence_quote: unlike the per-runtime permission settings, which are advisory
permission_model.note: Per-runtime permissions are advisory by default; enabling the srt sandbox provider gives a policy engine.

tracing.evidence_quote: Handles subprocess launch, JSON logging, session extraction, and exit classification.
tracing.note: Per-agent JSON logs plus attempt JSON records; `coral ui` dashboard.

replayability.evidence_quote: Git worktrees keep concurrent ideas separate and make every evaluated attempt reproducible.
replayability.note: Attempts re-gradable from commits; sessions resumable, but no trajectory replay engine.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: Some built-in graders (e.g. SWE-bench, terminal-bench) use [Harbor](https://github.com/corca-ai/harbor) to run evaluations inside Docker containers.

guardrails.evidence_quote:
every agent subprocess is wrapped by the configured
    sandbox provider (see ``coral.sandbox``), which enforces filesystem and
    network boundaries
guardrails.note: Also grader-separation: `.coral/private/` is hidden from agents to prevent eval hacking.

target_domain.evidence_quote: kernel and algorithm optimization, benchmark solving, machine-learning experiments, scientific discovery

open_source.evidence_quote: This project is released under the Apache 2.0 [LICENSE](LICENSE).

first_release_date.note: Basis: README release announcement; no tag list available.

stars.note: As stated in the pinned repository evidence header.
